title: Metric Critique: First Message Volume
scenario: The BooedUp product team wants to measure messaging engagement to understand relationship depth after users establish Matches or Wingman connections.
prompt: A stakeholder proposes tracking 'Total First Messages Sent' as the primary metric for messaging engagement. What is the significant flaw in this metric, and what should be measured instead?
instructions: One short sentence: name the flaw, propose a fix. Aim for under 20 words total.
expected_themes: not normalized per Match or Wingman connection
reference_answer: Should be normalized per connection. First Messages per Match (or per Wingman) is better.

grading_rubric.description: Answer states the metric is not normalized per Match/Wingman connection or per user
Suggests a denominator (e.g., Messages per Match, Messages per connection, Messages per active user)

grading_rubric.criterion: References the count vs rate distinction
grading_rubric.description: Explicitly or implicitly flags that total volume is a count metric vulnerable to cohort size changes

hints: Think about what happens if the number of Matches doubles—does the total go up for a good reason or a bad reason?
Consider whether you care about the absolute volume or the rate at which messages are sent given the number of opportunities.
What denominator would make this metric comparable across time periods with different cohort sizes?
common_mistakes: Proposing to segment by user demographic instead of normalizing per connection
Suggesting median instead of mean (not the main flaw here)
Critiquing 'first message' as too narrow without addressing the normalization issue
Proposing to track all messages instead of first messages (misses the count-vs-rate problem)
